title: The Jones-Collins Astoria Hot Eight recordings at Italian Hall
summary: He describes the Astoria band, its personnel, and giving each leader one of his tunes for the records.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I wanted to ask, before I forget it, something about those records you made. First of all, the Lee Collins records with Jones, which you made with Dave Jones too. Did you play with the band all the time at the end? Oh yeah.

I played with the band regularly. I played at the, the band used to play at this club right here where the post office is on Bienville. It was named the, I call it the club not so long ago we used to talk. Well anyway we were.
Not the one down with the river, but was that it down with the river?

No, it was right here, no, by this post office. Oh sure, yeah. Right across from there, the La Vida. The La Vida, yeah. Well we played there together, and then from there we went over to the Asturias. And we played over there Asturias and that's why we, we did the recording down here at the Italian Hall on Esplanade Street. And we had, we had our regular band, but we had Albert Morgan on bass. He wasn't playing with us, he was playing on a boat with Faith Marble, which he was a good piano player too at those times. Well we had, we had him on bass and then we had a white boy playing clarinet by the name of Sidney Arrigan. He played the clarinet on those records. And then most of the tunes that we used were my tunes and everybody had a, had a tune except him and I gave him one. I gave him one because I had gave Lee one and I gave Theta Poirnell one. And I kept one. And finally we had a, had a contract for royalties on these, on these records. And we got royalties and finally they, they released these on other records. They came back and they released them again. And so we had some royalties doing us because they sold them to two or three companies and everything. But we tried to, try to intercede and get them. And they told us that we could produce the contracts. They didn't have it on the book, but if we could produce the contract, they'd pay us the royalties. Well that's been better than 35 years ago. And nobody saved those contracts. And nobody's got a contract, you see. So it just, it just stopped us from getting the money. Which we, it seemed like we'd have got about five, six, maybe seven thousand dollars out of it.
